How to sew a small phone bag with a flap and inner pockets

A small lined pouch for a phone, money and cards: one T of two pieces folds into three pockets, a flap with a snap and two little ears. Watch it come together step by step.

Some links on this page are affiliate links. As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.

Overview

The finished pouch

A small lined pouch for a phone, money and cards: three pockets inside, a flap with a plastic snap and two little ears at the top. The chain is only an idea — there is none in the video; the ears take any chain or strap with clasps. Tap the pouch to take it apart.

  1. 1Outer — printed cotton · long piece 57 × 19 cm (22½ × 7½ in) and flap piece 31 × 13 cm (12¼ × 5⅛ in)
  2. 2Interfacing — fusible · the same two sizes, on the outer pieces only
  3. 3Lining — pink cotton · the same two sizes, no interfacing
  4. 4Flap — the 31 × 13 cm (12¼ × 5⅛ in) piece: round the bottom, up the back, round corners at its end
  5. 5Pockets ×3 — two in the accordion — lines 11 and 22 cm (4⅜ and 8⅝ in) from the fold, through both halves — and the third between it and the back: cards, money, phone
  6. 6Ears ×2 — 5 × 5 cm (2 in) squares, folded into a narrow strip, then into a loop
  7. 7Snap — plastic · in the middle of the flap, on the topstitching
  8. 8Seams — all 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) · a 6 cm (2⅜ in) opening opposite the flap, closed by the topstitching 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) all round

Step-by-step instructions

  1. From printed cotton cut the long piece, 57 × 19 cm (22½ × 7½ in), and the flap piece, 31 × 13 cm (12¼ × 5⅛ in).

    Cut the lining the same: 57 × 19 cm and 31 × 13 cm.

    Cut fusible interfacing the same two sizes — for the outer pieces only.

    For the ears cut two squares of printed cotton, 5 × 5 cm (2 × 2 in).

    Every seam allowance in this pouch is 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in).

  2. Lay the long outer piece and the outer flap piece wrong side up.

    Put the interfacing on them, glue side down, edge to edge, and iron it on.

    The lining pieces get no interfacing.

  3. Lay the long piece right side up.

    Put the flap piece on it face down, across the middle: its 13 cm (5⅛ in) end exactly in the middle of one long edge, level with it.

    Sew along that edge, 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) in, and open the flap piece out: the two pieces make a T.

    Make a T from the lining pieces the same way.

    Machine: straight stitch

  4. Put the lining T face down on the outer T, edges level, and clip them together.

    At the end of the flap piece, trace round any round object — a jar lid, a roll of tape — at both corners.

    Cut along the lines: the flap gets round corners.

  5. Start at one end of the opening: the 6 cm (2⅜ in) gap is in the middle of the long edge, opposite the flap piece.

    Sew all round the T, 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge, and stop at the other end of the opening.

    Clip into the two inner corners of the T — not through the stitching — and notch the round corners so they lie flat.

    Machine: straight stitch

  6. Pull the whole T out through the opening.

    Push out the corners and the round end of the flap.

    Press it flat, the raw edges of the opening tucked in.

  7. Stitch all round the edge, 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) in.

    Over the opening keep the tucked-in edges level: the topstitching closes it.

    Machine: straight stitch

  8. Turn the T lining side up.

    Fold the long piece in half, the lining inside: the fold goes through the middle of the flap piece, which folds in half along its length.

    With a tape measure mark 11 cm (4⅜ in) from the fold, then another 11 cm from that mark: lines 11 and 22 cm (4⅜ and 8⅝ in) from the fold. Draw them across with a ruler.

  9. Stitch along the first line, through both layers.

    Stitch along the second line the same way.

    Between the fold and the first line, and between the two lines, the halves make two loops.

    Machine: straight stitch

  10. Open the flap piece out flat.

    Flatten the long piece so that its middle — the fold — lies at the end of the flap piece and both seams go to the middle.

    It folds like an accordion: two pockets, one behind the other. The third comes in step 12.

  11. Fold the square in half and open it again.

    Fold both edges to that fold, then fold in half again: a narrow strip, four layers thick.

    Fold the strip in half into a little loop. Make two.

  12. Turn the flap piece over the pockets. Its fold is the bottom of the pouch and closes every pocket.

    The rest of it is the back; its end sticks out past the top — that is the flap. Between the back and the pockets is the third pocket.

    Slip an ear into each side near the top, between the back and the pockets, the loop sticking out.

    Clip the sides.

  13. Sew down one side right on the edge: through the back, the layer next to it and the ear. The folds of the accordion pockets stay free — the END VIEW shows where the stitching goes.

    Sew the other side the same way.

    Machine: straight stitch

  14. Set the first half of the snap in the middle of the flap's round end, on the line of topstitching.

    Fold the flap down over the front and mark where the snap lands.

    Set the second half there.

  15. The phone — into the pocket next to the back.

    Money — into the middle pocket.

    Cards — into the front pocket.

    Close the flap on the snap.

    Hook a chain or a strap with clasps onto the ears. There is none in the video — any one you like will do.

Good to know

Questions and answers

What size should I cut the fabric for a phone pouch?

For this pouch you cut two pieces of printed cotton — a long piece 57 × 19 cm (22½ × 7½ in) and a flap piece 31 × 13 cm (12¼ × 5⅛ in) — the same two of lining, the same two of fusible interfacing for the outer, and two 5 × 5 cm (2 in) squares for the ears. Every seam is 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in). The cutting diagram below shows it all.

Do I need interfacing for a phone pouch?

This one has light fusible interfacing on the two outer pieces only, cut the same sizes — 57 × 19 cm and 31 × 13 cm — and ironed onto the wrong side. The lining has none.

How do you make the pockets inside?

Fold the topstitched T in half across the long piece, lining inside, and sew two lines through both halves, 11 cm (4⅜ in) and 22 cm (8⅝ in) from the fold. Open it out: the seams go to the middle and the long piece folds like an accordion into two pockets. The flap piece then goes round the bottom and up the back: between it and the accordion is the third pocket, and its fold closes every pocket at the bottom. The phone goes next to the back, money in the middle, cards at the front.

Where do you leave the opening to turn it?

In the middle of the long piece's long edge, opposite the flap piece: leave 6 cm (2⅜ in) unsewn when you sew the two Ts together. Turn it right side out through the opening; the topstitching 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge all round closes it.

How do you put a plastic snap on the flap?

Set one half in the middle of the flap's round end, on the line of topstitching. Fold the flap down, mark where the snap lands on the front and set the other half there.

How do you make loops for a strap or chain?

From two 5 × 5 cm (2 in) squares: fold each into a narrow strip — in half, both edges to the fold, in half again — and then in half into a loop. Slip them into the sides near the top, between the back and the pockets, and stitch the sides right on the edge. There is no strap in the video; a chain or a strap with clasps fits the ears.
